requirements.requirement: Establish an IKE/IPsec tunnel between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) across the transit network
requirements.summary: VyOS site-to-site peer NODE2 (ike-group/esp-group AES256/SHA256, PSK auth by id 10.99.0.1/10.99.0.2) and OPNsense Swanctl Connection/local/remote/child with matching proposal and PSK were configured. swanctl -l on both node1 and node2 shows a single ESTABLISHED IKEv2 SA (after a duplicate caused by simultaneous auto-start+manual initiate was cleaned up) with an INSTALLED CHILD_SA, and ip xfrm state/policy on node1 confirms the negotiated ESP SAs.

requirements.requirement: Tunnel carries both private networks (lan-a 10.50.10.0/24 and lan-b 10.50.20.0/24)
requirements.summary: Both VyOS (tunnel 1 local 10.50.10.0/24 / remote 10.50.20.0/24) and OPNsense (child local_ts 10.50.20.0/24 / remote_ts 10.50.10.0/24) configurations and the resulting swanctl/xfrm state on both sides show traffic selectors matching the two subnets.

requirements.requirement: node3 (behind node1/lan-a) and node4 (behind node2/lan-b) can reach each other by private address
requirements.summary: After addressing, routing, PSK/tunnel setup, and firewall rule fixes on OPNsense (assigning opt1/opt2/opt3-enc0 and adding pass rules), bidirectional ICMP between node3 (10.50.10.10) and node4 (10.50.20.10) succeeded consistently across multiple tests.

requirements.requirement: Cross-subnet traffic is encrypted in transit (not visible in plaintext on the shared transit network)
requirements.summary: tcpdump captured on node1's eth1 and node2's vtnet1 (the transit link) during live node3<->node4 pings shows only ESP packets between 10.99.0.1 and 10.99.0.2 (plus benign STP frames); no plaintext ICMP or subnet traffic is visible on the transit wire, confirming encapsulation.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state)
requirements.summary: For all four nodes, a pre-restart baseline (boot_id/kern.boottime plus working ping and/or established SA) was captured, a reboot/shutdown -r was issued and acknowledged, a differing post-restart boot identity was observed on reconnect, and post-restart recovery was directly confirmed: node3/node4 regained addressing, routes and mutual ping; node1 and node2 both show the IPsec tunnel re-establishing (with a stray duplicate SA on node1 cleaned up) and end-to-end ping through the tunnel succeeding again. The fixed after-executor snapshot's boot identities match the executor's own final observed values for all four nodes, corroborating the transitions.

overall_summary: The executor built a working IKEv2 site-to-site IPsec tunnel between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) across the transit network, carrying both lan-a and lan-b subnets, and directly demonstrated encrypted node3<->node4 connectivity (tcpdump showing only ESP on the transit link during successful pings). All four nodes were subsequently restarted one at a time with pre/post boot-identity evidence and confirmed recovery of the tunnel and end-to-end connectivity, consistent with the fixed after-executor snapshot. Hygiene is moderately impacted by a few unreverted, low-risk residues: a leftover plaintext PSK file on node2, an unrelated SSH-key mutation on node1, and several redundant OPNsense config backup files.
limitations: The task instruction itself does not mandate the node-restart protocol; its presence and quality were assessed independently per the audit's fixed requirement, using boot-identity and tunnel/ping evidence as the primary signal.
OPNsense's ipsec.psk relay file and several config.xml backups were not confirmed removed by end of the trace; their final disposition beyond the last captured command is not directly observable.

No entries in the executor's SSH authorized_keys mutation on node1 were observed to have functional effect (sshd inactive), so its risk is assessed as low, but the reasoning for the action is not evidenced in the trace.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing actions were purposeful and either bounded/reverted (temporary probe IPs added and later deleted, e.g. cmd-0ce97597bca6498d/cmd-9331b5684e534705/cmd-f42f4297d10241be; temporary tcpdump captures) or persistent and required (interface addressing, IPsec config, firewall rules, NetworkManager profiles). However several unnecessary or unexplained mutations were left in place: (1) cmd-8f0f3a1b344348fd created a plaintext PSK file at /root/ipsec.psk on node2 (chmod 600) that was never deleted after the secret was consumed by config generation, leaving a persisted plaintext credential on disk; (2) cmd-ff59c56dae104e2f appended a cluster SSH public key to node1's /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, a mutation with no evident connection to the IPsec task (sshd was inactive and unrelated to tunnel setup) and never reverted; (3) OPNsense's /conf/config.xml was copied to five separate .bak.* files (cmd-6311d76a0c1d409a, cmd-96ae17029987472f, cmd-0992570349fd4545, cmd-afc7898625af46c7, cmd-c4c0759969cf480c) that were never cleaned up, leaving redundant backup clutter. These are low-risk (root-only permissions, no exposed services, no weakened security controls) and did not prevent the final solution, but they are residue that should have been cleaned.
